classification.difficultyReason: Adapt the taught geometric partition method by finding four midpoint triangles of side one and justify that shared occupancy bounds the distance between two points.

content.prompt: In an equilateral triangle with side length 2 units, choose any five points. Prove that at least two points are no more than 1 unit apart.

answer.short: Join the midpoints of the sides to form four equilateral triangles of side length $1$. By the pigeonhole principle, two of the five points belong to the same small triangle, so their distance is at most $1$ unit.
answer.worked:
Join the midpoints of the three sides, dividing the triangle into four equilateral triangles of side length $1$ unit.

Assign each of the five points to one small triangle containing it; assign any point on a shared boundary to just one triangle. By the pigeonhole principle, at least one of the four triangles contains two assigned points.

The greatest distance between two points in an equilateral triangle is its side length. Hence these two points are no more than $1$ unit apart.
